# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 49 (Bu-Vb Sk49)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk49
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 49. Sticking out the tongue

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 49 (*Jivhānicchāraka*) is a training rule from the *Vinaya Piṭaka* governing decorum during eating, translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali as "Sticking out the tongue" [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the sekhiya section regulating personal deportment, specifically proscribing monastics from sticking out their tongue while eating [SuttaCentral].

The rule corresponds to Sekhiya 49 of the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and both *Parivāra* lists [SuttaCentral]. Curated parallels on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is preserved extensively across early Buddhist schools, occurring in the Vinayas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus highlights extensive Pali-internal formulaic sharing between Sekhiya 49 and neighboring mealtime and deportment training rules in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, showing substantial character and segment overlap with Sekhiyas 44–48, 50, 52, 54, and 68 [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with the Tibetan *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104-2) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
